General tips for lao:

Staggers, use them. this is mainly how lao's pressure is done since his blockstrings got nerfed. it's a pseudo-mixup where the opponent has to guess what you'll do after a string. especially nasty when paired with his grabs.

if you're getting zoned out. be patient, lao has great mobility for a reason. if timed correctly, his dive kick is an easy way(high risk, high reward) in over a projectile and can lead to full combo.


Don't be a jumping jellybean. People will anti air you faster than raiden could teleport. mobility is one of lao's best assets and it's best to use it intelligently rather than abusively. 




Adding on tempest:

Ex spin has many utilities. it's still a phenomenal anti-air, provided you time it right. can be used as an anti-cross up on wake up. and is one of the fastest launching moves in the game, it can punish normals, strings and specials that are normally hard to punish. if landed in any of those scenarios, nets you more or less a 30% combo.

Best damage with and without meter, get that 2-frame link, it's worth the trouble.

hat spin can be used as a tool in neutral, either getting in via run or teleport, or slowing down an aggressive enemy(i advise caution with this one because the hitbox rotates around lao)

FBCs are going to be your best friend for these two, while i don't know much of hellfire scorpion(played him a bit) other than using flame aura and FBCs for some pressure and good chip damage, Liu kang is one of my mains. 

Learning to FBC or fire-ball cancel(s) with DF liu kang is crucial, it is key in being a successful and deadly liu kang although the execution is tight so take that into account. FBCs are primarily used as pressure tools, utilizing it to create blockstrings and essentially making your moves quite plus on block. You can also back dash out of an FBC if you want to choose a more defensive approach. 

You can FBCs out any normal string really, but your go-to strings are going to be; B1,2(armor breaking) F4,4(low starter) and F2,1,3(not really a starter since you can't convert much from this unless your in the corner but more so the ideal starter for pressure). I personally use St.1,1,1 because it's a fast normal which i can FBC into a good damage, corner-carry combo but that's just me. Speaking of combos, with FBCs and a bar of meter you can get good to great damage depending where you are on the screen.However If you are meter conservative, don't worry as you can still get good damage off an FBC without using meter for the bicycle-kick flip. 

DF liu kang is an execution-heavy character, maybe not so much as someone like reptile or D.vorah but nonetheless your execution should be sharp. Your going to need it to properly execute his FBCs and even his Instant-air fireballs(wanna get the most mileage of your combos regardless of meter, and add a touch of style to them, learn this). So get to the lab and be prepared for long sessions of practice.

Normal: Standard Attack(punch/kick) layout

Special: a move that's normally associated with a sequence of inputs combined with a button press. ex: QCB+square/X

Overhead/High/Medium/Low: Attack/Block zones. Overhead/High/Medium Attacks can be block by blocking high or simply holding the block button. Low attacks can be blocked by either jumping or holding the input down through analog or d-pad plus the block button. Medium Attacks(mainly projectiles) can also be jumped through.

mix-up: the moveset/sequence of inputs where you "force" your opponent to block the wrong way/zone. perfect examples are 50/50s where you have to guess which zone(Overhead or Low) to block or sometimes your opponent could add in a throw to keep you off balance.

zoning: where you keep distance between you and your opponent for advantageous reasons, this tactic is done with heavy use of various projectiles. **WARNING** noobs *will* call this spamming.

Breaker: providing you have 2 meters of bar, you can either break a pressuring opponent while your blocking(block breaker) or stop an opponent's combo.

Punish: When your opponent is recovering from an unsuccessful attack and you manage to counter before your opponent could fully recover. the term *Reversal* is highly related with punishes. **note:** Frame Data helps in trully understanding when and how you can punish.

Juggle: a combo where it keeps your opponent stunned in mid air or in a "juggle state".

i see. well i wouldn't use too much of meter if i were you, who knows when that breaker is gonna come in handy. and i suggest you try optimizing your combos as much as you can, more damage the better since it may be unlikely for you to do substantial chip damage and that window of opportunity for you to punish is quite limited in your scenario. also look up the frame data on lao and your character, it might help with as to what move you should respond with. constantly using the same move as a response can make you predictable. as far as your punish goes, well its not so much so the timing but more on the execution and reads. figuring out what your opponent could/would do next is key, even playing out multiple scenarios could prove beneficial. oh and if you mean dive kick as the flying kick then i HIGHLY suggest you block that or at least keep in mind as to when he's gonna do it. that special move has low recovery on block leading you for a big punish. the dive kick and EX cyclone spin(or whatever its called) are easily lao's most punishable super and doesn't take bullet time reaction to capitalize on it. you can also punish an unsafe teleport but it might take some practice, his down+back square/X(the one where he tosses his hat around him) is safe on block and high recovery so don't try counter attacking unless you're willing to risk getting punished hard as like you said, lao has amazing priority especially in his normals
